titel: Dominus ac Redemptor — the brief of suppression (21 July 1773)
quelle: Latin after Augustin Theiner, Clementis XIV. Pont. Max. Epistolae et Brevia (Paris, 1852), doc. CCCXVII, whose paragraph numbering is carried as the citation grid; Internet Archive scan, OCR emended against the sense. Public domain (brief of 1773; edition 1852).
hinweis: The corpus's closing text, complete: the brief by which Clement XIV suppressed the Society of Jesus on 21 July 1773 — the apparatus ends, deliberately, here. The English is this site's unofficial machine-generated working translation, made directly from the Latin; no full public-domain English translation was located, and none was consulted — cite the Latin. Not yet part of the concordance index.

sections.blurb: Forty-odd numbered paragraphs: the long recital of precedents, the grounds, the operative suppression, and the provisions for persons and property.

units.orig: Dominus, ac Redemptor noster, Jesu Christus, Princeps pacis a Propheta praenuntiatus , quod hunc in mundum veniens per angelos primum pastoribus significavit, ac demum per se ipsum, antequam in caelos ascenderet , semel et iterum suis reliquit discipulis ; ubi omnia Deo Patri reconciliavisset , pacificans per sanguinem crucis suae , sive quae in terris , sive quae in caelis sunt, Apostolis etiam reconciliationis tradidit ministerium , posuitque in eis verbum reconciliationis , ut legatione fungentes pro Christo, qui non est dissensionis Deus, sed pacis, et dilectionis , universo Orbi pacem annuntiarent , et ad id potissimum sua studia conferrent ac labores , ut omnes in Christo geniti solliciti essent servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis, unum corpus et unus spiritus, sicut vocati sunt in una spe vocationis, ad quam nequaquam pertingitur ut inquit S. Gregorius Magnus, si non ad eam unita cum proximis mente curatur.
units.en: Our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, foretold by the Prophet as the Prince of Peace — which, coming into this world, he made known first to the shepherds through angels, and at the last, before he ascended into heaven, left once and again himself to his disciples — when he had reconciled all things to God the Father, making peace through the blood of his cross for whatever is on earth and whatever is in heaven, entrusted to the Apostles also the ministry of reconciliation and placed in them the word of reconciliation, so that, serving as ambassadors for Christ — who is not a God of dissension but of peace and of love — they might announce peace to the whole world, and might above all direct their labours and endeavours to this: that all who are begotten in Christ should be careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace, one body and one spirit, even as they were called in the one hope of their calling — to which, as Saint Gregory the Great says, there is no attaining at all unless one strives toward it with a mind united to one's neighbours.

units.orig: Hoc ipsum potiori quadam ratione Nobis divinitus traditum reconciliationis verbum , et ministerium, ubi primum, meritis prorsus imparibus , evecti fuimus ad hanc Petri Sedem , irt memoriam revocavimus, die, noctuque prae oculis habuimus, cordique altissime inscriptum gerentes , ei pro viribus satisfacere contendimus , divinam ad id opem assidue implorantes , ut cogitationes , et consilia pacis Nobis , et universo Dominico gregi Deus infundere dignaretur ad eamque consequendam tntissimum Nobis, firmissimumque aditum reserare. Quinimo probe scientes, divino Nosconsilio constitutos fuisse super gentes, et super regna , ut in excolenda vinea Sabaoth , conaervandoque Christianae Religionis aedificio , cujus Christus est anguiaris lapis, evellamus, et destruamus, et disperdamus, et dissipemus, et aedificemus, et plantemus, eo semper fuimus animo , constantique voluntate , ut quemadmodum pro Christianae Reipublicae quiete , et tranquillilate nihil a Nobis praetermittendum esse censuimus , quod plantando, aedificandoque esset qnovis modo acconimodatum; ita, eodeni mutuae charitatis vinculo expostulante , ad evellendum , destruendumque quidquid jucundissimum etiam Nobis esset , atque gratissimum , et quo carere minime possemus sine maxima animi molestia , et dok)re, prompti aeque essemus, atque parati.
units.en: This very word and ministry of reconciliation, divinely committed to Us with the greater force, We called to mind as soon as We were raised — with merits entirely unequal to it — to this See of Peter; We have kept it before our eyes day and night, and bearing it inscribed deep in our heart We have striven to answer to it with all our strength, imploring the divine help unceasingly, that God might deign to pour thoughts and counsels of peace into Us and into the whole flock of the Lord, and to open to Us the safest and firmest way of attaining it. Knowing well, moreover, that We have been set by God's counsel over nations and over kingdoms so that, in tilling the vineyard of Sabaoth and preserving the edifice of the Christian religion whose cornerstone is Christ, We might root up and pull down, scatter and destroy, and build and plant, We have ever been of this mind and constant will: that as We have judged that nothing must be neglected by Us for the quiet and tranquillity of the Christian commonwealth which could in any way serve for planting and building, so — when the same bond of mutual charity demands it — We should be equally prompt and prepared to root up and destroy even what is most pleasing and most dear to Us, and what We could scarcely lose without the greatest distress and sorrow of mind.

units.orig: Non est sane ambigendum, ea inter quae ad Catholicae Reipublicae bonum, felicitatemque comparandam plurimum conferunt, principem fere locum tribuendum esse Regularibus Ordinibus, ex quibus amplissimum in universam Christi Ecclesiam quavis aetate dimanavit ornamentum , praesidium , et utilitas. Hos idcirco Apostolica haec Sedes approbavit nonmodo, suisque fulcita est auspiciis, verum etiam pluribus auxil beneficiis, exemptionibus, privilegiis et facultatibus , ut ex his aid pietatem excolendam , et Religionem, ad populorum mores verbo et exemplo rite informandos , ad Fidei unitatem inter fideles servandam , confirmandamque , magis magisque excitarentur, atque inflammarentur. Ast ubi eo res devenit , ut ex aliquo Regulari Ordine, vel non amplius uberrimi ii fructus , atque optatissima emolunienta a Christiano populo perciperentur, ad quae afferenda fuerant primitus instituti , vel detrimenlo potius esse visi f uerint , ac pertuifbandsei magis populorum tranquitlitati, quam eidem procurand» accommodati ; haec eadem Apostolica Sedes , quae eisdem plantandis operam impenderat suam, suamquc intiposuerat auctoritatem , eos vel novis communire legibus , vel ad pristinam vivendi severitatem revdcare, vel penitus etiam evellere , ac dissipare minime dubitavit.
units.en: It is surely beyond doubt that among the things which contribute most to procuring the good and the happiness of the Catholic commonwealth, almost the first place must be given to the regular orders, from which in every age the amplest ornament, protection and profit have flowed out upon the whole Church of Christ. For this reason this Apostolic See has not only approved them and supported them with its patronage, but has also enriched them with many benefits, exemptions, privileges and faculties, so that they might be more and more stirred and inflamed to cultivate piety and religion, to form the morals of the peoples rightly by word and example, and to preserve and confirm the unity of the faith among the faithful. But when things have come to such a pass that from some regular order those most abundant fruits and most desired advantages for which it was first instituted were no longer received by the Christian people, or that it seemed rather to be a detriment, and fitter to disturb the tranquillity of the peoples than to procure it, this same Apostolic See — which had spent its labour on planting them and had lent them its authority — has never hesitated either to fortify them with new laws, or to recall them to their original severity of life, or even to root them out and disperse them altogether.

units.orig: Hac sane de causa Innocentius Papa III. Praedecessor noster cum comperisset nimiam Regularium ordinum diversitatem gravem in Eoclesiam Dei confusionem inducere, in Conciliogenerali Lateranensi IV, firmiter prohibuit, ne quis de cetero novam Religionem inveniat ; sed quicumque ad Religionem converti voluerit unam de approbatis assumat; decrevitque insuper, ut qui voluerit religiosam domum de novo fundare, regulam, et institutionem accipiat de approbatis. Unde consequens fuit ; ut non liceret omnino novam Religionem instituere sine speciali Romani Pontificis licentia , et merito quidem; nam cuni novffi Congregationes majoris perfectionis gratia instituantur, prius ab hac sancta Apostolica Sede ipsa vitae futurae forma examinari , et perpendi debet diligenter, ne sub specie majoris boni , et sanctioris vitai plurima in Ecclesia Dei incommoda, et fortasse etiam mala exoriantur.
units.en: For this very cause Innocent III, our predecessor, when he had found that the excessive diversity of the regular orders was bringing grave confusion into the Church of God, firmly forbade in the Fourth Lateran general council that anyone thereafter should devise a new religious institute; whoever wished to be converted to religion was to take up one of those approved; and he decreed further that whoever wished to found a religious house anew should receive a rule and institute from those approved. Whence it followed that it was in no way lawful to institute a new religious order without the special licence of the Roman Pontiff — and with good reason: for since new congregations are instituted for the sake of greater perfection, the form of their future life ought first to be examined and weighed diligently by this holy Apostolic See itself, lest under the appearance of a greater good and a holier life very many inconveniences, and perhaps even evils, arise in the Church of God.

units.orig: Quaravis vero providentissime haec fuerint ab fnnocentio lll. Praedecess. nostro constituta , tamen postmodum non solum ab Apostolica Sede importuna petentium inhiatio aliquorum Ordinum Regularium approbationem extorsit , verum etiani nonnullorum praesumptuosa temeritas diversorum Ordinum praecipue Mendicantium nondum approbatorum effrenatam quasi multitudinem adinvenit. Quibus plene cognitis, ut malo statim occurreret, Gregorius Papa X. pariter Praedecessor noster in generali Concilio Lugdunensi renovata Constitutione ipsius Innocentii III. Praedecessoris districtius inhibuit , ne aliquis de cetero novum Ordinem, aut Religionem adinveniat, vel habitum novae Religionis assumat. Cunctas vero generaliter Religiones, et Ordines Mendicantes post Concilium Lateranenae IV. adinventos, qui nullam confirmationem Sedis Apostolicaee meruerunt, perpetuo probibuit, Confirmatos autem , ab Apostolica Sede modo decrevit subsistere infrascripto : ut videlicet profssoribus eorumdem Ordinum ita liceret in illis remanere, si voluerint, quod nullum deinceps ad eorum professionem admittercnt , nec de novo domum , vel aliquem locum acr quirerent, nec domos, seu loca , quae habebant alienare valerent sine ejusdem S. Sedis licentia speciali. Ea enim omnia dispositioni Sedis Apostolicae reservavit in Terrae sanctae subsidium , vel pauperum , vel alios pios usus per locorum Ordinarios, vel eos , quibus S. Sedes ipsa commiserit, convertenda. Personis quoque ipsorum Ordinum omnino interdixit quoad extraneos praedicationis , et audiendi confessiones officium, aut etiam sepulturam. Declaravit tamen in hac Constitutione minime comprehensos esse Prfledicatorum et Minorum Ordines, quos evidens ex eis utiiitas Ecolesiae universali proveniens perhibuerat approbatos. Voluitque insuper Eremitarum S. Augustini , et Carmelitarum Ordines in solido statu permanere, ex eo quod istorum institutio praedictum generale Concilium Lateranenae praecesserat. Demum sin- 25. giilaribus porsonis Ordinum, ad quos haec Constitutio extendebalur . transeundi ad reliquos Ordines approbatos licentiam concessit generalem ; ita tamen , ut nullus Ordo ad .alium , vel Gonventus ad Conventum se, ac loca sua totaliter transferret , non obtenta prius speciali Sedis Apostolicffi licentia.
units.en: But although these things had been most providently established by Innocent III our predecessor, nevertheless afterwards not only did the importunate craving of petitioners extort from the Apostolic See the approval of certain regular orders, but the presumptuous rashness of some devised an almost unbridled multitude of different orders, chiefly mendicant, not yet approved. When this was fully known, Gregory X, likewise our predecessor, that he might meet the evil at once, renewed in the general council of Lyons the constitution of Innocent III and more strictly forbade anyone thereafter to devise a new order or religious institute, or to assume the habit of a new institute. All religious institutes and mendicant orders generally, devised after the Fourth Lateran council, which had earned no confirmation from the Apostolic See, he prohibited in perpetuity; those confirmed by the Apostolic See he decreed should subsist only in the manner following: namely, that the professed of those orders might remain in them, if they wished, on condition that they admit no one further to their profession, acquire no new house or place, and have no power to alienate the houses or places they held without the special licence of the same Holy See. For he reserved all these things to the disposition of the Apostolic See, to be converted to the aid of the Holy Land, or to the poor, or to other pious uses, through the ordinaries of the places or those to whom the Holy See itself should commit it. To the persons of those orders he entirely forbade, as regards those outside, the office of preaching and of hearing confessions, and burial also. He declared, however, that the orders of Preachers and Minors were by no means comprehended in this constitution, since the evident benefit coming from them to the universal Church had shown them approved. He willed moreover that the orders of the Hermits of Saint Augustine and of the Carmelites remain in solid state, because their institution had preceded the said Lateran general council. Finally, to individual persons of the orders to which this constitution extended he granted a general licence of passing to the other approved orders — yet so that no order might transfer itself wholly to another, or convent to convent, with its places, without first obtaining the special licence of the Apostolic See.

units.orig: Hiscemet vestigiis secundum temporum circumstantias inhffiserunt alii Romani Pontifices Praedecessores nostri, quorum omniuni decreta longum esset referre. Inter caeteros vero Glemens Papa V. pariter Praedecessor noster per suas sub plumbo 6 nonas Maii anno Incarnationis Dominicae 1312. expcditas litteras Ordinem Militarcm Templariorum nuncupatorum , quamvis legitime confirmatum, et alias de Ghristiana Republica adeo praeclare meritum, ut a Sede Apostolica insignibus beneficiis, privilegiis, facultatibus, exemptionibus, licentiis cumnlatus fuerit, ob universalem diffamationem suppressit, et totaliter extinxit , etiamsi Concilium generale Viennenae , qui negotium examinandum commiserat , a formali , et definitiva ferenda sententia censuerit se abstinere.
units.en: In these same footsteps, according to the circumstances of the times, followed other Roman Pontiffs our predecessors, whose decrees it would be long to recount. Among the rest, Clement V, likewise our predecessor, by his letters under lead expedited the sixth of the nones of May in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1312, suppressed and totally extinguished the military order called of the Templars — although it had been lawfully confirmed, and had otherwise deserved so excellently of the Christian commonwealth that it had been laden by the Apostolic See with signal benefits, privileges, faculties, exemptions and licences — on account of its universal defamation; even though the general council of Vienne, to which he had committed the examination of the affair, judged that it should abstain from pronouncing a formal and definitive sentence.

units.orig: Sanctus Pius V, similiter Praedecessor noster, cujus insignem sanctitatem pie colit, et veneratur Ecclesia Catholica, Ordinem Regularem Fratrum Humiliatorum Concilio Lateranensi anteriorem, approbatumque a felicis recordationis Innocentio III, Honorio III, Gregorio IX, et Nicolao V, Romanis Pontificibus Praedecessoribus itidem nostris, ob inobedientiam decretis Apostolicis , discordias domesticas, et externas exortas, nullum omnino futuree virtutis specimen ostendentem , et ex eo quia aliqui ejusdem Ordinis in necem S. Caroli S. R. E. Cardinalis Borromei Protectoris ac Visitatoris Apostolici dicli Ordinis scelerate conspiraverint , extinxit , ac penitus abolevit
units.en: Saint Pius V, likewise our predecessor, whose eminent holiness the Catholic Church devoutly honours and venerates, extinguished and utterly abolished the regular order of the Humiliati Brothers — older than the Lateran council, and approved by Innocent III, Honorius III, Gregory IX and Nicholas V of happy memory, Roman Pontiffs likewise our predecessors — for disobedience to apostolic decrees, for domestic and external discords that had arisen, because it gave no promise whatever of future virtue, and because certain men of that order wickedly conspired to murder Saint Charles Borromeo, Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, protector and apostolic visitor of the said order.

units.orig: Recolendae memoriae Urbanus Papa VIII, etiam Praedecessor noster, per suas in simili forma Brevis die 6 februarii 1626. expediias litteras Congregationem Fratrum Conventualium Reformatorum a felicis memoriae Sixto Papa V. itidem Praedecessore nostro solemniter approbatam , et pluribus beneficiis , ac favoribus auctam , ex eo quia ex praedictis Fratribus ii in Ecclesia Dei spirituales fructus non prodierint , imo quamplures differentiae inter eosdem Fratres conventuales Reformatos , ac Fratres Conventuales non Reformatos ortae fue rint, perpetup suppressit, ac extinxit : Domus, Gonventus , loca , supellectilem, bona, res, actiones, et jura ad prasdictam Congregationem spectantia, Ordini Fratrum Minorum S. Frandsci Gonventualium concessjt, et assignavit, exceptis tantum domo Neapolitana, et domo Sancti Antonii de Padua nuncupata de Urbe quam postremam Camerae Apostolicae applicavit , et incorporavit , suseque suorumque suorumque successorum dispositioni reservavit : Fratribus denique praedictae suppressae Congregationis ad Fratres S. Francisci Gappuceinos, seu de obaervantia nuncupatos transitum permisit.
units.en: Urban VIII, of honoured memory, also our predecessor, by his letters in like form of Brief expedited the 6th of February 1626, perpetually suppressed and extinguished the Congregation of the Reformed Conventual Brothers, solemnly approved by Sixtus V of happy memory, likewise our predecessor, and enriched with many benefits and favours — because from those brothers spiritual fruits had not come forth in the Church of God, and indeed very many differences had arisen between the Reformed Conventual Brothers and the Conventual Brothers not Reformed. The houses, convents, places, furnishings, goods, effects, actions and rights belonging to the said congregation he granted and assigned to the Order of Friars Minor Conventual of Saint Francis, excepting only the Neapolitan house and the house of Rome called of Saint Anthony of Padua, which last he applied and incorporated to the Apostolic Camera, and reserved to his own disposition and that of his successors; and to the brothers of the said suppressed congregation he permitted passage to the Brothers of Saint Francis called Capuchins, or those of the Observance.

units.orig: Idem Tlrbanus Papa VIIL per alias suas in pari forma Brevis die 2. decembris 1643, expeditas litcras Ordinem Regularem Sanctorum Ambrosii , et Barnabae ad Nemus perpetuo suppressit, extinxit, et abolevit, subjecitque Hegulares praedicti suppressi Ordinis jurisdictioni, et correctioni Ordinariorum locorum, praedictisque Regularibus licentiam concessit se transferendiad alios Ordines Regulares Apostolica Sede approbatos. Quam suppressionem rec, memoria; Innocentius Papa X. Praedecessor quoque noster solemniter per suas sub plumbo Kal. Aprilis anno Incarnatioms Dominicae 1 645 expeditas litteras confirmavit j et insuper Beneficia , Domos , et Monasteria praedicti Ordinis, quae antea regularia erant, ad saecularitatem reduxit, ac in posterum saecularia fore , et esse declaravit.
units.en: The same Urban VIII, by other letters of his in equal form of Brief expedited the 2nd of December 1643, perpetually suppressed, extinguished and abolished the regular Order of Saints Ambrose and Barnabas ad Nemus, subjected the regulars of the said suppressed order to the jurisdiction and correction of the ordinaries of the places, and granted the said regulars licence to transfer themselves to other regular orders approved by the Apostolic See. This suppression Innocent X of honoured memory, also our predecessor, solemnly confirmed by his letters under lead expedited the Kalends of April in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1645; and moreover he reduced to the secular state the benefices, houses and monasteries of the said order, which before were regular, and declared that they should thereafter be secular.

units.orig: Idemque Innocentius X. Praedecess. noster persuas in simili forma Bre vis die 1 6 martii 1 645 , ob graves perturbationes excitatas inter Regulares Ordinis Pauperum Matris Dei Scholarum Piarum, etsi Ordo ille prffivio maturo examine a Gregorio Papa XV. Praedecessore nostro solemniter approbatus fuerit , praefatum Regularem Ordinem in simplicem Congregationem, absque ullorum votorum emissione , ad instar instituti Congregationis Presby terorum saecularium Oratorii in Eeclesia S. Mariae in Valiicella de Urbe S. Philippi Neri nuncupatae, reduxit : Regularibus praedicti Ordinis sic reducti transitum ad quamcumque Religionem approbatam concessit : admissionem Novitiorum , et admissorum professionem interdixit : superioritatemdenique, et jurisdictionem , quae penes Ministrum generalem , Visitatores , aliosque Superiores residebat, in Ordinarios locorum totaiiter transtulit : quae omnia per aliquot annos consecuta sunt effectum, donec tandem Sedes haec Apostolica , cognita praedicti Instituti utilitate , illum ad pristinam votorum solemnium formam revocavit, ac in perfectum Regularem Ordinem redegit.
units.en: And the same Innocent X, our predecessor, by his letters in like form of Brief of the 16th of March 1645, on account of the grave disturbances stirred up among the regulars of the Order of the Poor of the Mother of God of the Pious Schools — although that order, after previous mature examination, had been solemnly approved by Gregory XV our predecessor — reduced the said regular order to a simple congregation without the taking of any vows, after the pattern of the institute of the Congregation of secular priests of the Oratory in the church of Santa Maria in Vallicella in Rome, called of Saint Philip Neri; granted the regulars of the order so reduced passage to any approved religious institute; forbade the admission of novices and the profession of those admitted; and finally transferred wholly to the ordinaries of the places the superiority and jurisdiction which had resided with the minister general, the visitors and the other superiors. All of which took effect for some years, until at length this Apostolic See, having recognised the usefulness of the said institute, recalled it to the original form of solemn vows and restored it to a perfect regular order.

units.orig: Per similes suas in pari forma Brevis die 29 octobris 1050, expeditas litteras idem Innocentius X. Praedecess. noster ob discordias quoque et dissensiones exortas suppressit totaliter Ordinem S. Basilii de Armenis : regulares praedicti suppressi Ordinis omnimode jurisdictioni, et obedientiae Ordinariorum locorum subjecit in habitu Clericorum saecularium , assignata iisdm congrua sustentatione ex redditibus Conventuum suppressorum : illisque etiam facultatem transeundi ad quancumque Religionem approbatam concessit.
units.en: By his like letters in equal form of Brief expedited the 29th of October 1650, the same Innocent X our predecessor, likewise because of discords and dissensions that had arisen, totally suppressed the Order of Saint Basil of the Armenians; he subjected the regulars of the said suppressed order in every way to the jurisdiction and obedience of the ordinaries of the places, in the habit of secular clerics, a suitable maintenance being assigned to them from the revenues of the suppressed convents; and he also granted them the faculty of passing to any approved religious institute.

units.orig: Pariter ipae InnocentiusX. Praedecess. noster per aliassuas indicta fornia Brevis die 22 junii 1661 , expeditas litteras attendens nullos spirituales fructus ex regulari Gongregatione Presbyterorum Boni Jesus in Ecclesia sperari posse, prsfatam Gongregationem perpetuo cxtinxit : Regulares prsdictos jurisdictioni Ofdinariorum Locorum subjecit, assignata eisdem congrua sustentatione ex redditibus suppressffi Gongregationis, et cum facultate transeundi ad quemlibet Ordinem rularem approbatum a Sede Apostolica; suoque arbitrio reservavit applicationem bonorum prffidicts Congregationis iu alios pios usus.
units.en: Likewise the same Innocent X our predecessor, by other letters of his in the said form of Brief expedited the 22nd of June 1651, considering that no spiritual fruits could be hoped for in the Church from the regular Congregation of the Priests of the Good Jesus, extinguished the said congregation in perpetuity; subjected the said regulars to the jurisdiction of the ordinaries of the places, a suitable maintenance being assigned them from the revenues of the suppressed congregation, and with the faculty of passing to any regular order approved by the Apostolic See; and reserved to his own judgement the application of the goods of the said congregation to other pious uses.

units.orig: Denique felicis recordationis Clemens Papa IX. Praedecessor itidem noster cum animadverteret, tres regulares Ordines, Ganonicorum videlicet regularium Sancti Georgii in Alga nuncupatorum , Hieronymianorum de Fesulis ac tandem Jesuatorum a Sancto Johanne Columbano institutorum parum. vel nihil utilitatis et commodi Christiano populo afferre , aut sperare posse eos esse aliquando allaturos, de iis supprimendis, extinguendisque consiliumcepit, idque perfecit suis litteris in simili forma Brevis die 6 decembris 1668 expeditis, corumque bona, et redditus satis conspicuos, Yenetorum Republica postulante, in eos sumptus impendi voluit, qui ad Gretenae bellum adversus Turcas sustinendum erant neoessario subeundi.
units.en: Finally Clement IX of happy memory, likewise our predecessor, when he had observed that three regular orders — namely the Canons Regular of Saint George in Alga, the Hieronymites of Fiesole, and lastly the Jesuati founded by Saint John Colombini — brought little or nothing of usefulness or advantage to the Christian people, nor could be hoped ever to bring it, took counsel to suppress and extinguish them, and carried it out by his letters in like form of Brief expedited the 6th of December 1668; and their goods and quite considerable revenues, at the petition of the Republic of Venice, he willed to be spent on those burdens which had of necessity to be undertaken to sustain the Cretan war against the Turks.

units.orig: In his vero onmibus decemendis , perficiendisque satius semp duxeint Praedecessores nostri ea uti consultissima agendi ratione, quam ad intercludendum penitus aditum animorum contentionibus, et ad quaelibet amovenda dissidia , vei partium studia magis conferre existimarunt. Hinc molestaiila , ac plenanegotii prstermissa methodo, quae in forensibus instituendis judiciis adhiberi consuevit , prudentis legibus unice inhaerentes, ea potestatis plenitudine quatamquam Christi in terris Vicarii , ac supremi Christianae Reipublicae moderatores amplissime donati sunt, rem omnem absolvendam curarunt, quin regularibus Ordinibus suppressioni destinatis, veniam facarent , et facultatem sua experiundi jura at gravissimas illas vel propulsandi criminationes , vel causas amoliendi , ob quas ad illud consilii genus suscipiendum adducebantur.
units.en: In deciding and carrying through all these things, our predecessors judged it always better to employ that most well-advised manner of proceeding which they considered more apt to close off altogether every opening for contentions of spirit, and to remove all disputes and partisanships whatsoever. Hence, setting aside that laborious and business-laden method which is customarily employed in the conduct of judicial proceedings, and adhering solely to the laws of prudence, they took care to settle the whole matter by that fullness of power with which, as Vicars of Christ on earth and supreme moderators of the Christian commonwealth, they are most amply endowed — without granting the regular orders destined for suppression leave and faculty to try their rights, or to repel those most grave accusations, or to remove the causes on account of which they were led to adopt that kind of counsel.

units.orig: Hisigitur, aliisque maxinii apud omnes ponderis, et auctoritatis exemplis Nobis ante oculos propositis , vehemcntique simul flagrantes cupiditate ut in ea, quam infra aperiemus, deliberatione fidenti animo , tutoque pede incedamus , nihii diligentiae omisimus , et inquisitionis , ut quidquid ad regularis Ordinis , qui Societatis Jesu vulgo dicitur j originem pertinet , progressum , hodiernumque statum perscrutaremur et compertum inde habuimus, eum ad animarum salulem, ad haereticorum , et maxime Infidelium conversionem , ad inajus denique pietatis, et religionis incrementum a Sancto suo Conditore fuisse institutum ; atque ad optatissimum flnem facilius feliciusque consequendum , arctissimo Evangelicffi paupertatis voto tam in communi , quam in particulari fuisse Deo consecratum , exceptis tan-' tununodo studiorum , seu litterarum CoUegiis, cpiibus possidendi redditus ita facta est vis , et potestas y ut nihil tamen ex iis redditibus in ipsius Societatis commodum, utilitatem, ac usum impendi unquam possit, atque converti.
units.en: With these and other examples of the greatest weight and authority before our eyes, and burning at the same time with a vehement desire to walk with confident mind and sure foot in the deliberation We shall disclose below, We omitted no diligence and no inquiry in searching out whatever pertains to the origin, the progress and the present state of the regular order commonly called the Society of Jesus; and We found thereby that it was instituted by its holy founder for the salvation of souls, for the conversion of heretics and above all of the infidels, and finally for the greater increase of piety and religion, and that, the more easily and happily to attain that most desired end, it was consecrated to God by the strictest vow of evangelical poverty, in common as well as in particular — excepting only the colleges of studies or letters, to which the power and capacity of possessing revenues was so given that nothing of those revenues might ever be spent or converted to the advantage, use or benefit of the Society itself.

units.orig: His, aliisque sanctissimis legibus probata primum fuit eaden Societas Jesu a rec. memoriae Paulo Papa III. Praedecessore nostro per suas sub plumbo 5. kal. octobris anno Incarnationis Dominics 1 540 , expeditas litteras , ab eodemque concessa ei fuit facultas condendi jura; atque statuta, quibus Societatis praesidio, incolumitati , atque regimini firmissime consuleretur. Et quamvis idem Paulus Praedecessor Societatem ipsam angustissimis sexaginta dumtaxat alumnorum limitibus ab initio circumscripsisset; per alias tamen suas itirdem sub plumbo pridie kal. martii anno Incarnationis Dominicae 1 543, expeditas litteras locum dedit eadem in Societate iis omnibus quos in eam excipere iilius moderatoribus visum fuisset opportunum , ait necessarium. Anno deinde 1549, suis in simili forma Brevis die 15 novembris expeditis litteris idem Paulus Praedecessor pluribus , atque amplissimis privilegiis eamdem Societatem donavit , ac in his indul- tum alias per eumdem Praepositis generalibus dicts Societatis con- cessum admittendi viginti Presbyteros Coadjutores spirituales, eisque impertiendi easdem facultates, gratiam, et auctoritatem , quibus Socii ipsi professi donantur, ad alios quoscunque, quos idoneos fore iidem Praepositi generales censuerint , ullo absque limite , et numero cxtendendum voluit, atque mandavit 3 ac prsterea Societatem ipsam, et universos illius Socios, et personas, iilorumque bona qua&cunque ab omni superioritate , jurisdictione , correctione quorumcunque Ordinariorum exemit, et vindicavil, ac sub sua, et Apostolicae Sedis protectione suscepit.
units.en: Under these and other most holy laws the same Society of Jesus was first approved by Paul III of honoured memory, our predecessor, by his letters under lead expedited the 5th of the Kalends of October in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1540, and by the same was granted to it the faculty of framing laws and statutes by which the protection, safety and government of the Society should be most firmly provided for. And although the same Paul our predecessor had at the beginning confined the Society within the very narrow limit of no more than sixty members, yet by other letters of his likewise under lead, expedited the day before the Kalends of March in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1543, he made room in the same Society for all whom its moderators should judge it opportune or necessary to receive into it. Then in the year 1549, by his letters in like form of Brief expedited the 15th of November, the same Paul our predecessor endowed the same Society with many and most ample privileges — and among them willed and commanded that the indult, granted before by him to the superiors general of the said Society, of admitting twenty priests as spiritual coadjutors and of imparting to them the same faculties, grace and authority as are given to the professed members themselves, be extended without any limit or number to any others whomsoever whom the same superiors general should judge fit; and moreover he exempted and set free the Society itself, and all its members and persons, and all their goods whatsoever, from all superiority, jurisdiction and correction of any ordinaries whomsoever, and took them under his own protection and that of the Apostolic See.

units.orig: Haud minor fuit reliquorum Praedecessorum nostrorum eadem erga Societatem liberalitas, ac munificentia. Constat enim a rec. memoriae Julio III, Paulo IV, Pio IV et V, Gregorio XIII, Sixto V, Gregorio XTV, Clemente VIII, Paulo V, Leone XI, Gregorio XV, Urbano VIII, aliisque Romanis Pontificibus privilegia eidem Societati jam anteatributa, vel confirmata fuisse , vel novis aucta accessionibus, vel apertissime declarata. Ex ipso tamcn ApostoUcarum Consliturlionum tenorc, et verbis palam coliigitur cadem in Societate suo fere ab initio varia dissidiorum , ac aemulationum semina pullulasse , ipsos non modo inter Socios , verum etiam cum aliis regularibus Ordinibus Clero saeculari , Academiis , Universitatibus , publicis litterarum Gymnasiis, et cum ipsisetiam Principibus, quorum in ditionibus Societas fuerat excepta; easdemque contentiones , et dissidia excitata modo fuisse de votorum indole , et natura , de tempore admittendoram Sociorum ad vota de facultate Socios expeliendi , de iisdeni Sociis ad sacros ordines promovendis sine congrua , ac sine votis solemnibus contra Concilii Tridentini , ac sanctae menioriee Pii Papae V. Praedecessoris nostri decreta ; modo de absoluta potestate , quam Praepositus generalis ejusdem Societatis sibi vindicabat , ac de aiiis rebus ipsius Societatis regimen spectantibus; modo de variis doctrinae capitibus, de scholis, de exemptionibus, et privilegiis, quae Locorum Ordinarii, aliaeque personae in Ecdesiastica vel saeculari dignitate constituts suse noxia esse jurisdictioni , ac juribus contendebant; ac demum minime defuerunt gravissimae accusationes eisdem Sociis objectae , quae Christianae Reipublicae pacem , ac tranquillitatem non paruni perturbarunt.
units.en: No less was the liberality and munificence of the rest of our predecessors toward the same Society. For it is well known that by Julius III, Paul IV, Pius IV and V, Gregory XIII, Sixtus V, Gregory XIV, Clement VIII, Paul V, Leo XI, Gregory XV, Urban VIII of honoured memory, and by other Roman Pontiffs, the privileges already bestowed on the same Society were either confirmed, or increased with new additions, or most plainly declared. Yet from the very tenor and words of the apostolic constitutions it is openly gathered that in the same Society, almost from its beginning, various seeds of dissensions and rivalries sprouted — not only among the members themselves, but also with other regular orders, with the secular clergy, with academies, universities and public schools of letters, and even with the princes in whose dominions the Society had been received; and that these contentions and disputes were stirred up now about the character and nature of the vows, about the time of admitting members to vows, about the faculty of expelling members, about promoting members to sacred orders without a title and without solemn vows contrary to the decrees of the Council of Trent and of Pius V our predecessor of holy memory; now about the absolute power which the superior general of the same Society claimed for himself, and about other matters touching the government of the Society; now about various heads of doctrine, about schools, about exemptions and privileges which the ordinaries of the places and other persons constituted in ecclesiastical or secular dignity contended were injurious to their jurisdiction and rights; nor, lastly, were there wanting most grave accusations brought against the same members, which disturbed not a little the peace and tranquillity of the Christian commonwealth.

units.orig: Multffihinc ortae adversus Societatera querimonise, quae nonnullorum etiam Principum auctoritate munitae ac relationibus ad recol. memoriae Paulum IV, Pium V, et Sixtum V, Praedecessores nostros delatae fuerunt. In his fuit clarae memoriae Philippus II, Hispaniarum Hex Catholicus, qui tum gravissimas, quibus ille vehementer impellebatur rationes, tum etiam eos, quos ab Hispaniarum Inquisitoribus adversus immoderata Societatis privilegia, ac regiminis formam acceperat clamores et contentionum capita a nonnullis ejusdem etiam Societatis viris doctrina, et pietate spectatissimis confirmata, eidem Sixto V. Praedecessori exponenda curavit , apud eumdemque egit , ut Apostolicam Societatis visitationem decernerct, atque committeret.
units.en: Hence arose many complaints against the Society which, fortified by the authority of certain princes as well, were laid before Paul IV, Pius V and Sixtus V, our predecessors of honoured memory. Among these was Philip II, the Catholic King of the Spains, of illustrious memory, who took care to lay before the same Sixtus V our predecessor both the most weighty reasons by which he was urged, and the complaints which he had received from the inquisitors of the Spains against the immoderate privileges of the Society and its form of government, together with the heads of contention confirmed by some men of the same Society most distinguished for learning and piety; and he pressed upon him that he should decree and commission an apostolic visitation of the Society.

units.orig: Ipsius Philippi Regis petitionibus , et studiis , quae sunmia inniti aequitate animadverterat , annuit idem Sixtus Praedecessor, delegitque ad Apostolici Visitatoris munus Episcopum prudentia, virtute et doctrina omnibus commendatissimum , ac praeterea congregationem designavit nonnullorum S. R. E. Cardinalium , qui ei rei perficiendae sedulam navarent operam. Verum dicto Sixto V. Praedecessore immatura morte praerepto , saluberrimum ab eo susceptum consilium evanuit, omnique caruit effectu. Ad supremum autem Apostolatus apicem assumptus felicis recordationis Gregorius PP. XIV per suas litteras sub plumbo 4. kal. julii anno Dominicae Incarnationis 1591. expeditas,Societatis Institutum amplissime iterum approbavit rataque haberi jussit , ac firma privilegia quaecumque eidem Societati a suis Praedecessoribus collata; et illud prae ceteris, quo cautum fuerat, ut a Societate expelli , dimittique possent Socii , forma judiciaria minime adhibita , nulla scilicet praemissa inquisitione , nullis confectis actis nullo ordine judiciario servato , nullisque terminis y etiam substantialibus servatis, sola facti veritate inspecta; culpffi, vel rationabilis causae tantum ratione habita, ac personarum , aliarumque circumstantiarum. Altissimum insuper silentium imposuit , vetuitque sub poena potissimum exconmiunicationis latae sententiae, ne quis dictae Societatis Institutum , constitutiones , aut decreta directe , vel indirecte impugnare auderet, vel aliquid de iisquovis modo immutari curaret. Jus tamen cuilibet reliquit , ut <|uidquid addendum , minuendum, aut immutandum cenaeret sibi tantummodo , e Romanis solum Pontificibus pro tempore existentibus vel immediate, vel per Apostolicae Sedis Legatos , seu Nuncios significare posset , atque proponere.
units.en: The same Sixtus our predecessor assented to the petitions and endeavours of King Philip, which he had observed to rest on the highest equity, and chose for the office of apostolic visitor a bishop most commended to all for prudence, virtue and learning, and moreover designated a congregation of several Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church who should devote their diligent labour to carrying the matter through. But the said Sixtus V our predecessor being snatched away by an untimely death, the most salutary design he had undertaken vanished and was without any effect. Raised then to the supreme summit of the apostolate, Gregory XIV of happy memory, by his letters under lead expedited the 4th of the Kalends of July in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1591, again most amply approved the Institute of the Society and ordered that all privileges whatsoever conferred on the same Society by his predecessors be held ratified and firm — and, before the rest, that one by which it had been provided that members might be expelled and dismissed from the Society without any judicial form, that is, with no previous inquiry, no drawing up of acts, no judicial order observed, no terms even substantial observed, on inspection of the truth of the fact alone, account being taken only of the fault or of a reasonable cause, and of the persons and other circumstances. He imposed moreover the deepest silence, and forbade, above all under pain of excommunication latae sententiae, that anyone should dare to attack the Institute, constitutions or decrees of the said Society directly or indirectly, or should endeavour to have anything about them changed in any way; leaving nevertheless to everyone the right to signify and propose whatever he should judge ought to be added, diminished or changed, but only to himself and to the Roman Pontiffs for the time being, either immediately or through the legates or nuncios of the Apostolic See.

units.orig: Tantum vero abest, ut hsec omnia satis fuerint compescendis adversus Societatem clamoribus, et querelis, quin potius magis, magisque universum fere Orbiem pervaserunt molestissimae contentiones de Societatis doctrina, quam fidei veluti Orthodoxae bonisque moribus repugnantem plurimi traduxeruiit ; domesticae etiam, externaeque efferbuerunt dissensiones, et frequentiores factae sunt in eam , de nimia potissimum terrenorum bonorum cupiditate accusationes : ex quibus onmibus suam hauserunt originem tum perturbationes illae omnibus satis cognit» , quae Sedem Apostolicam ingenti moerore affecerunt , ac molestia ; tum capta a Principibus nonnullis in Societatem consilia. Quo factum est , ut eadem Societas novam Instituti sui , ac privilegiorum confirmationem a felicis recordationis Paulo Papa V. Praedecessore nostro impetratura , coacta fuerit ab eo petere , ut rata habere vellet, suaque confirmare auctoritate decreta quaedam in quint/i generali Gongregatione edita , atque ad verbum exscripta in suis sub plumbo pridie non. septembris anno Incarnationis Dominicae 1606. desuper expeditislitteris,quibusin decretis discretissime legitur, tam internas Sociorum simultates ac turbas , quam exterorum in Societatem querelas ac postulationes Socios in comitiis congregalos impulisse ad sequens condendum statutum : Quoniam Societas nostra, quae ad fidei propagationem , et animarum iucra a Domino excitataest, sicut per propria Instituti ministeria, quae spiritualia arma sunt, cum Ecclesiae utilitate , ac proximorum sedificatione sub crucis vexillo finem feliciter consequi potest , quem intendit , ita et haec bona impediret, et se maximis periculis exponeret , si ea tractet, quae saecularia sunt, et ad res politicas atque ad status gubernationem pertinent; idcirco sapientissime a nostris majoribus statutum est , ut militantcs Deo aliis quae a nostra professione abhorrent non implicemur. Cum autem his praesertim temporibus valde periculosis, pluribus locis et apud varios Principes (quorum tamen amorem, et charitatem sanctae memoriae Pater Ignatius conservandam ad divinum obsequium pertinere putavit ) aliquorum fortasse culpa , et vel ambitione , vel indiscreto zelo Religio nostra male audiat et alioquin bonu Christi odor necessarius sit ad fructificandum ; censuit Congregatio ab omni specie mali abstinendum esse , et querelis , quoad fieri poterit, etiam ex falsis suspicionibus provenientibus, occurrendum. Quare praesenti decreto graviter, et severe nostris onmibus interdicit, ne in hujusmodi publicis negotiis , etiam invitati , aut allecti ulia ratione se immisceant, nec ullis precibus , aut suasionibus ab instituto deflectant. Et praeterea quibus efficacioribus remediis omnino huic morbo , sicubi opus sit , medicina adhibeatur, patribus Definitoribus accurate decernendum , et definiendum commendavit.
units.en: But so far were all these things from sufficing to quiet the outcries and complaints against the Society that rather the most troublesome contentions spread more and more over almost the whole world — concerning the doctrine of the Society, which very many denounced as repugnant to the orthodox faith and to good morals; dissensions domestic and external boiled up; and the accusations against it multiplied, above all of excessive greed for earthly goods. From all of which took their origin both those disturbances well enough known to all, which brought the Apostolic See great sorrow and trouble, and the measures which certain princes adopted against the Society. So it came about that the same Society, when it would obtain a new confirmation of its Institute and privileges from Paul V of happy memory our predecessor, was compelled to ask of him that he would ratify and confirm with his authority certain decrees published in the fifth general congregation and transcribed word for word into his letters expedited thereon under lead the day before the Nones of September in the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1606; in which decrees it is most plainly read that it was as much the internal quarrels and disturbances of the members as the complaints and demands of outsiders against the Society that drove the members gathered in assembly to enact the following statute: 'Since our Society, which the Lord has raised up for the propagation of the faith and the winning of souls, can happily attain by the proper ministries of its Institute, which are spiritual arms, under the standard of the cross, with benefit to the Church and edification of neighbours, the end at which it aims, so also it would both hinder these goods and expose itself to the greatest dangers if it should handle the things that are secular and that pertain to politics and the government of states; therefore it was most wisely established by our elders that, warring for God, we should not be entangled in other things abhorrent to our profession. And since especially in these most perilous times, in many places and with various princes — whose love and charity Father Ignatius of holy memory thought it belonged to the divine service to preserve — our religious institute may perhaps through the fault of some, and either through ambition or indiscreet zeal, be ill spoken of, while the good odour of Christ is otherwise necessary for bearing fruit, the congregation has judged that we must abstain from every appearance of evil, and must meet complaints as far as may be, even those proceeding from false suspicions. Wherefore by the present decree it gravely and severely forbids all of ours to involve themselves in public affairs of this kind by any means, even if invited or drawn in, or to swerve from the Institute for any entreaties or persuasions. And further it has commended to the father definitors to determine and define with care by what more efficacious remedies a medicine may be applied wholly to this disease, wherever there be need.'

units.orig: Maximo sane animi nostri dolore obaervavimus , tam praedicta , quam alia complura deinceps adhibita remedia nihil ferme virtutis prs se tulisse , et auctoritatis ad tot , ac tantas evellendas dissipandasque turbas, accusationes, et querimonias in saepe dictam Societatem , frustraque ad id laborasse caeteros Praedecessores nostros Urbanum VIII, Clementem IX, X, XI et XII, Alexandrum VII et VHI, Innocentium X, XI, XII et XIII, et Benedictum XIV. qui optatissimam conati sunt Ecclesiae restituere tranquillitatem plurimis salubcrrimis editis Constitutionibus; tam circa saecularia negotia, sive extra sacras Missiones , sive earum occasione minime exercenda , quani circa dissidia gravissima, ac jurgia adversus Locorum Ordinarios, rcgulares Ordines , Loca pia, atque Communitates cujusvis generis in Europa , Asia, et America, non sine ingenti animarum ruina, ac populorum admiratione a Societate acriter excitata -, tum etiam super interpretatione , et praxi Ethnicorimi quorumdam rituum aliquibus in locis passim adhibita, omissis iis, qui ab Universali Ecclesia sunt ritc. probati ; vel super earum sententiarum usu , et interpretatione, quas Apostolica Sedes tanquam scandalosas , optimaeque morumdisciplins manifeste noxias merito proscripsit; vel aliis demum super rebus maximi equidem momcnti , et ad Christianorum dogmatum puritateni sartam tectam servandam apprime necessariis, etex quibus nostra hac non minus, quam superiori aetate plurima dimanarunt detrimenta , et incommoda ; perturbatioiies nimirum ac tumultus in nonnullis CathoUcis regionibus; Ecclesia) persecutiones in quibusdain Asiae , et Europae provinciis ; ingens deniquc allatus est moeror Praedeoessoribus nostris, et in his piae memoriae Innocntio Papae XI. qui nccessitate compulsus eo dovcnit , ut Societati interdixerit novitios ad habitum admittere; tum Innocentio Paps XIII. qui eamdem poenam coactus fuit eidem comminari; ac tandem recol. memoriae Benedicto Papae XIV. qui visitationem Domorum , Collegiorumque in ditione charissimi in Christo.filii nostri Lusitaniae et Algarbiorum Regis Fidelissimi existentium censuit decernendam; quin ullum subinde vel Sedi Apostolicae solamen , vel Societati auxilium , vel ChristianaB Reipublicae bonum accesserit ex uovissimis Apostolicis litteris a fdicis recordationis Clemente Papa XIII. immediato Prffidecessore nostro extortis potius , ut verbo utamur a Praedecessore nostro Gregorio X in supracitato Lugdunensi GEcumenico Conciiio adhibito, quam impetratis , quibus Societatis Jesu Institutum magnopere commendatur ac rursus approbatur.
units.en: With the greatest sorrow of our soul We have observed that both the aforesaid and many other remedies applied thereafter carried almost no force or authority to uproot and scatter so many and so great troubles, accusations and complaints against the oft-named Society, and that our other predecessors laboured in vain to this end — Urban VIII, Clement IX, X, XI and XII, Alexander VII and VIII, Innocent X, XI, XII and XIII, and Benedict XIV — who endeavoured to restore to the Church her longed-for tranquillity by publishing many most salutary constitutions: whether concerning secular business, not to be engaged in either outside the sacred missions or on their occasion; or concerning the most grave quarrels and disputes sharply stirred up by the Society against the ordinaries of the places, the regular orders, pious places and communities of every kind in Europe, Asia and America, not without immense ruin of souls and astonishment of the peoples; or again about the interpretation and practice of certain heathen rites employed here and there in various places, to the omission of those which the universal Church rightly approves; or about the use and interpretation of those maxims which the Apostolic See has deservedly proscribed as scandalous and manifestly injurious to good morals; or finally about other matters of the greatest moment and altogether necessary for preserving intact the purity of Christian doctrine, from which in our own age no less than in the former very many detriments and inconveniences flowed: disturbances, namely, and tumults in some Catholic countries, persecutions of the Church in certain provinces of Asia and Europe; and lastly great grief was brought to our predecessors, and among them to Innocent XI of pious memory, who, compelled by necessity, went so far as to forbid the Society to admit novices to the habit; then to Innocent XIII, who was forced to threaten it with the same penalty; and finally to Benedict XIV of honoured memory, who judged that a visitation must be decreed of the houses and colleges lying in the dominions of our most dear son in Christ the Most Faithful King of Portugal and the Algarves; nor did there thereafter accrue any comfort to the Apostolic See, any help to the Society, or any good to the Christian commonwealth from the latest apostolic letters — extorted rather than obtained, to use the word which our predecessor Gregory X employed in the above-cited ecumenical council of Lyons — from Clement XIII of happy memory, our immediate predecessor, in which the Institute of the Society of Jesus is greatly commended and approved anew.

units.orig: Post tot, tantasque procellas , ac tempestates acerbissimas futurum optimus quisque sperabat, ut optatissima illa tandem aliquando illucesceret dies , quae tranquiiiitatem , et pacem esset cumulatissime allatura. At Petri Cathedram gul)emante eodem Clemente XIII. Praedecessore longe difficiliora ac turbulentiora accesserunt tempora Auctis enim quotidie magis in praedictam Societatem ciamoribus, ei querelis , quinimo periculosissimis alicubi exortis seditionibus, tumultibus, dissidiis et scandalis, quae, Christianae charitatis vinculo lat>e-r factato , ac penitus disrupto, fidelium animos ad partiumstudia odia et inimicitias vehementer inflammarunt , eo discriminis, ac pericuii res perducta visa est , ut ii ipsi , quarum avita pietas , ac in Societatem liberaiitas haereditario quodam veluti jure a majoribus accepta omnium fere linguis sununoiere commendatur, charissimi nemp in Christo fiiii nostri Reges Francorum , Hispaniarum , Lusitanise, ao utriusque Siciliae suis ex Regnis, ditionibus, atque provinciis Socios dimittere coacti omnino fuerint, et expellere; hoc unum putantes extremum tot malis superesse remedium , et penitus necessarium ad impediendum, quominus Christiani populi in ipso sanctae MatrisEc clesiae sinu sese invicem lacesserent , provocarent, lacerarent.
units.en: After so many and so great storms and most bitter tempests, every good man hoped that that most longed-for day would at length dawn which should bring tranquillity and peace in fullest measure. But under the government of the same Clement XIII our predecessor upon the Chair of Peter, times far more difficult and more turbulent supervened. For as the outcries and complaints against the said Society daily increased, and indeed as most perilous seditions, tumults, discords and scandals broke out in some places, which — the bond of Christian charity being loosened and utterly torn apart — vehemently inflamed the minds of the faithful to partisanship, hatred and enmity, the danger and peril seemed brought to such a point that those very princes whose ancestral piety and liberality toward the Society, received as it were by hereditary right from their forebears, is praised by almost every tongue — namely our most dear sons in Christ the Kings of France, of the Spains, of Portugal and of the Two Sicilies — were absolutely compelled to dismiss and expel from their kingdoms, dominions and provinces the members of the Society, judging this one extreme remedy to remain against so many evils, and altogether necessary to prevent the Christian peoples from challenging, provoking and rending one another in the very bosom of holy Mother Church.

units.orig: Ratum vero habentes praedicti charissimi in Christo fiiii nostri remediumhoc firmum esse non posse, ac Universo Christiano Orbi reconciiiando accommodatum , nisi Societas ipsa prorsus extinguerer tur, ac ex integro supprimeretur ; sua idcirco apud praefatum Clementem PP. XIII. Praedecessorem exposuemnt studia , ac voiuntatem , et qua vaiebant auctoritate, et precibus, conjunctis simui votis exposiularunt , ut efficacissima ea ratione perpetuae suorum sulxliiorum securiiaii , universaeque Cliristi Eccicsiae hom provideniissime coiisu- lerent. Qui tamen praeter omnium expectationem contigit ejusdem Pontificis obitus rei cursum, exiiumque prorsus impcdivii, Hinc Nobis in eadem Petri Caihedra, divina disponente Clementia, constitutis esedeni statim oblatae sunt preces , petitiones , et vota, quibus sua quoquc addiderunt studia, animique sententiam Episcopi complures, aliique viri dignitate , doctrina, religione piurimum conspicui.
units.en: But the said our most dear sons in Christ, holding it certain that this remedy could not be firm, nor apt to reconcile the whole Christian world, unless the Society itself were utterly extinguished and suppressed entire, laid their desires and their will before the said Clement XIII our predecessor, and with what authority and entreaties they could, their petitions joined together, demanded that he would by this most efficacious means make provident and final provision for the perpetual security of their subjects and for the good of the universal Church of Christ. But the death of the same Pontiff, falling out contrary to the expectation of all, wholly impeded the course and issue of the affair. Hence, when We had been placed by the disposing divine Clemency upon the same Chair of Peter, the same prayers, petitions and desires were at once laid before Us; and to them very many bishops, and other men most conspicuous for dignity, learning and religion, added their own endeavours and the judgement of their minds.

units.orig: Ut autem in re tam gravi tantique momenti tutissimum caperemus consilium, diuturno Nobis temporis spacio opus esse judicavimus, non modo ut diligenter inquirere, maturius expendere, et consultissime deliberare possemus , verum etiam ut multis gemitibus, et continuis precibus singulare a Patre luminumexposcremus auxiliuni, et praesidium -, qua etiam in re Fidelium omnium precibus, pietatisque operibus Nos saepius apud Deum juvari curavimus. Perscrutari inter caetera voluimus , quo innitatur fundamento pervagata illa apud plurimos opinio , Religionem scilicet Clericorum Societatis Jesu fuisse a Concilio Tridentino solenmi quadam ratione approbatam , et connrmatam ; nihilque aliud de ea actum fuisse comperimus in citato Concilio , quam ut a generali illo exciperetur decreto , quo de reliquis regularibus Ordinibus cautum fuit , ut finito tempore novitiatus , novitii qui idonei inventi fuerint ad profitendum admittantur , aut a Monasterio ejiciantur. Quamobrem eadem sancta synodus (Sess. 25, c. 16, de Regular. ) declaravit se nolle aliquid innovare aut prohibere, quin prajdicta religio Clericorum Societatis Jesu , juxta pium eorum Institutum a Sancta Sede Apostolica approbatum , Domino et ejus Jilcclesiae inaervire possit.
units.en: That in a matter so grave and of such moment We might take the safest counsel, We judged that We needed a long space of time, not only that We might inquire diligently, weigh maturely and deliberate most advisedly, but also that with many groanings and continual prayers We might beg from the Father of lights his singular help and protection; in which matter We also took care to be aided often before God by the prayers and works of piety of all the faithful. We willed among other things to search out on what foundation rests that opinion spread among very many, that the religious institute of the Clerks of the Society of Jesus was in some solemn manner approved and confirmed by the Council of Trent; and We found that nothing else was done concerning it in the said council than that it was excepted from that general decree by which it was provided, for the other regular orders, that at the end of the time of novitiate the novices found fit should be admitted to profession or dismissed from the monastery. Wherefore the same holy synod (Session 25, chapter 16, On Regulars) declared that it did not wish to make any innovation or prohibition that would prevent the said religious institute of the Clerks of the Society of Jesus, according to their pious Institute approved by the holy Apostolic See, from being able to serve the Lord and his Church.

units.orig: Tot itaque, ac tam necessariis adhibitis mediis , Divini Spiritus, utconfidimus, adjuti praesentia, etaffiatu, necnon muneris nostri compulsi necessitate , quo et ad Christianee Reipublicae quietem et tranquillitatem conciliandam , fovendam, roborandam, et ad illa omnia penitus de medio tollenda , quae eidem detrimento vel minimo esse possunt, quantum vires sinunt, arctissime adigimur; cumque praeterea animadverteremus praedictam Societatem Jesu uberrimos illos, amplissimosque fructus, etutilitates afferre ampliusnon posse, ad quos instituta fuit, a tot Praedecessoribus nostris approbata , ac plurimis omata privilegiis, imo fieri , aut vix , aut nullo modo posse , ut ea incolumi manente vera pax , ac diuturna Ecclesiae restituatur ; his propterea gravissimis adducti causis, ahisque pressi rationibus quas et prudentiae leges , et optimum Universalis Ecclesiae regimen Nobis suppeditant , altaque mente repositas ser/amus, vestigiis inhaorentes eorumdem Praedecessorum nostrorum , et praesertim memorati Gregorii X. Praedecess. nostri in generali Concilio Lugdunensi, cum et nunc de Societate agatur, tum Instituti sui , tum privilegiorum etiani suorum ratione , Mendicantium Ordinum numero ascripta , maturo consilio , ex certa scientia , et plenitudine potestatis Apostolicae saepedictam Societatem extinguimus, et supprimimus; tollimus , et abrogamus omnia, et singula ejus officia, ministeria et administrationes, domus, scholas, collegia, hospitia, gymnasia, et loca quaecumque quavis in provincia, regno, et ditione existentia, et modo quolibet ad eam pertinentia; ejus statuta, mores, consuetudines , decreta, constitutiones , etiam juramento , confirmatione Apostolica , aut alias roboratas } omnia item , et singula privilegia , et indulta generalia , vel specialia , quorum tenores praesentibus , ac si de verbo ad verbum essent incerta, ac etiamsi quibusvis formulis, clausulis irritantibus , et quibuscumque vinculis et decretis sint concepta , pro plene et sufficienter expressis haberi volumus. Ideoque declaramus cassatam perpetuo manere, ac penitus extinctam omnem, et quamcumque auctoritatem Praepositi Generalis , Provincialium , Visitatorum, aliorumque quorumlibet dictae Societatis Superiorum tam in spiritualibus , quam in temporalibus; eamdemque jurisdictionem, et auctoritatem in Locorum Ordinarios totaliter, et omnimode transferimus , juxta modum casus, et personas, et iissubconditionibus, quas infra explicabimus; prohibentes quemadmodum per praesentes prohibemus , ne ullus amplius in dictam Societatem excipiatur, et ad habitum , ac novitiatum admittatur; qui vero hactenus fuerunt excepti, ad professionem votorum simplicium , vel solemnium , sub poena nullitatis admissionis , et professionis , aliisque arbitrio nostro, nullo modo admitti possint, et valeant. Quinimo volumus, praecipimus, et mandamus ut qui nunc tyrocinio actu vacant, statim, illico, immediate, et cum affectu dimittantur; ac similiter vetamus, ne qui votorum simplicium professionem emiserunt , nulloque sacro Ordine sunt usque adhuc initiati possint ad majores ipsos Ordines promoveri praetextu, aut titulo vel Jam emissae in Societate professionis vel privilegiorum contra Goncilii Tridentini decreta eidem Societati collatorum.
units.en: Having therefore employed so many and so necessary means, aided, as We trust, by the presence and inspiration of the Divine Spirit, and compelled also by the necessity of our office, by which We are most strictly bound, so far as our strength allows, both to procure, foster and strengthen the quiet and tranquillity of the Christian commonwealth, and to remove utterly from its midst whatever can be even the least detriment to it; and since We have moreover observed that the said Society of Jesus can no longer bring forth those most abundant and most ample fruits and benefits for which it was instituted, approved by so many of our predecessors, and adorned with so many privileges, and that indeed it can hardly or not at all come to pass that, the Society remaining unharmed, the true and lasting peace of the Church be restored: moved therefore by these most grave causes, and pressed by other reasons which the laws of prudence and the best government of the universal Church supply to Us, and which We keep stored deep in our mind, following in the footsteps of the same our predecessors, and especially of the said Gregory X our predecessor in the general council of Lyons — since the present matter also concerns a Society reckoned, both by reason of its Institute and by reason of its privileges, among the mendicant orders — with mature counsel, of our certain knowledge and out of the fullness of apostolic power, WE EXTINGUISH AND SUPPRESS THE OFT-NAMED SOCIETY: We take away and abrogate each and all of its offices, ministries and administrations, houses, schools, colleges, hospices, gymnasia and places whatsoever, in whatever province, kingdom or dominion existing and in any way belonging to it; its statutes, usages, customs, decrees and constitutions, even though strengthened by oath, apostolic confirmation or otherwise; likewise each and all of its privileges and indults, general or special, the tenors of which We will to be held as fully and sufficiently expressed in these presents as if they were inserted word for word, howsoever conceived in whatever formulas, clauses of annulment, bonds and decrees. And therefore We declare that all and every authority of the superior general, the provincials, the visitors and any other superiors whatsoever of the said Society, in spiritual as in temporal things, remains for ever annulled and utterly extinguished; and We transfer that same jurisdiction and authority wholly and in every way to the ordinaries of the places, according to the cases and persons and under the conditions which We shall explain below; forbidding, as by these presents We do forbid, that anyone henceforth be received into the said Society, or admitted to its habit and novitiate; and those hitherto received may in no way be admitted to the profession of simple or of solemn vows, under pain of the nullity of the admission and profession, and other penalties at our discretion. Moreover We will, enjoin and command that those who are now actually in their novitiate be dismissed at once, forthwith, immediately and effectively; and We likewise forbid that those who have made profession of simple vows and have not yet been initiated into any sacred order may be promoted to those major orders under the pretext or title either of a profession already made in the Society, or of privileges conferred on the same Society contrary to the decrees of the Council of Trent.

units.orig: Quoniam vero eo nostra tendunt studia, ut quemadmodum Ecclesiae utilitatibus . ac populorum tranquillitati consulere cupimusj itasingulis ejusdem Religionis individuis, seu Sociis, quorum singuiares personas paterne in Domino diligimus, solamen aliquod, et auxilium afferre studeamus, ut ab omnibus, quibus hactenus vexati fuerunt contentionibus, dissidiis, et angoribus liberi, fructuosius vineam Domini possint excolere, et animarum saluti uberius prodesse; ideo decernimus, et constituimus, ut Socii professi votorum duntaxat simplicium, et sacris Ordinibus nondum initiati, intra spatium temporis a Locorum Ordinariis definiendum, satis congruum ad munus «aliquod vel officium, vel benevolum receptorem inveniendum, non tamen uno anno longius a data praesentium nostrarum litterarum iuchoandum,Domibus et Gollegiis ejusdem Societatis omni votorum simplicium vinculo soluti egredi omnino debeant, eam vivendi rationem suscepturi, quam singulorum vocationi, viribus , et conscientis magis aptam in Domino judicaverint , cum et juxta Societatis privilegia dimitti ab ea hi poterant non alia de causa prsier eam , quani Superiores prudentiae, et circumstantiis magis conformem putarent, nulla praemissa citatione, nullis confectis actis, nulloque judiciario ordine servato.
units.en: But since our endeavours aim at this, that, as We desire to provide for the interests of the Church and the tranquillity of the peoples, so We may also strive to bring some comfort and help to the individual members of the same religious institute, whose persons We love paternally in the Lord, that, freed from all the contentions, disputes and anxieties by which they have hitherto been harassed, they may cultivate the vineyard of the Lord more fruitfully and profit more richly the salvation of souls: We therefore decree and ordain that the members professed of simple vows only, and not yet initiated into sacred orders, must depart from the houses and colleges of the same Society, released from every bond of their simple vows, within a space of time to be fixed by the ordinaries of the places — sufficient for finding some employment or office, or a benevolent receiver, yet not to begin later than one year from the date of these our present letters — to take up that manner of life which each shall judge in the Lord most suited to his vocation, his strength and his conscience; since indeed by the Society's own privileges they could be dismissed from it for no other cause than such as the superiors judged more conformable to prudence and circumstances, with no previous citation, no acts drawn up, and no judicial order observed.

units.orig: Omnibus autem Sociis ad sacros Ordines promotis veniam facimus, ac potestatem, easdem Domos, aut Gollegia Societatis deferendi , vel ut ad aliquem ex regularibus Ordinibus a Sede Apostolica approbatis se conferant , ubi probationis tempus a Goncilio Tridentino praescriptum debebunt explere , si votorum simplicium professionem in Societate emiserint , si vero solemnium etiam votorum per sex tantum integros menaes in probatione stabunt, super quo benigne cum eis dispensamus , vel ut in saeculo maneant tamquam Presbyteri , et Glerici Saeculares sub omnimoda, ac totali obedientia, et subjectione Ordinariorum , in quorum dioecesi domicilium figant ; decernentes insuper, ut his , qui hac ratione in saeculo manebunt congruum aliquod, donec provisi aliunde non fuerint, assignetur stipendium ex redditibus domus , seu GoUegii , ubi morabantur, habito tamen respectu tum reddituum, tum onerum eidem annexorum.
units.en: To all members promoted to sacred orders We give leave and power either to leave the same houses and colleges of the Society and betake themselves to some one of the regular orders approved by the Apostolic See — where, if they made profession of simple vows in the Society, they will have to complete the time of probation prescribed by the Council of Trent; but if of solemn vows also, they shall stand in probation for only six full months, wherein We benignly dispense with them — or to remain in the world as priests and secular clerics, under the entire and total obedience and subjection of the ordinaries in whose diocese they fix their domicile; decreeing further that to those who shall thus remain in the world there be assigned, until they are otherwise provided for, some suitable stipend out of the revenues of the house or college where they dwelt, regard being had both to the revenues and to the burdens annexed to them.

units.orig: Professi vero in sacris Ordinibus jam constituti , qui vel timore ducti non satis honestae sustentationis ex defectu , vel inopia congruae , vel quia loco carent ubi domicilium sibi comparent , vel ob provectam atatem, infirmam valetudinem, aliamque justam , gravemque causam, domus Societatis, seu Gollegia derelinquere opportunum minime existimaverint, ibidem manere poterunt ea tamen lege, ut nullam praedictae domus , seu GoUegii administrationem habeant. Glericorum Saecularium veste tantummodo utantur, vivantque Ordinario ejusdem loci plenissime subjecti. Prohibemus autem omnino quominug in eorum qui defident locum, alios sufficiant; Domum de novo juxta Goncilii Lugdunensis decreta seu aliquem locum acquirant; domos insuper, res, et loca, quae nunc habent , alienare valeant; quinimo in imam tantum domum , seu plures , habita ratione Socionun , qui remanebunt, poterunt congregari, ita ut domus, qu» vacuse relinquentur possint in pios usus converti juxta id quod sacris canonibus, voluntati fiindatorum, divini cultus incremento , animarum saluti, ac jpublicae utilitati videbitur suis loco , et tempore recte, riteque accommodatum. Interim vero vir aliquis ex Glero Saeculari prudentia; probisque moribus praeditus designabitur, qui dictaruni domorum praesit regimini , deleto penitus et suppresso nomine Societatis.
units.en: But the professed already constituted in sacred orders who — whether led by fear of not having honourable maintenance enough, or through lack of a suitable provision, or because they have no place where to find a domicile, or by reason of advanced age, infirm health, or another just and grave cause — shall judge it inopportune to leave the houses or colleges of the Society, may remain there; yet on this condition, that they have no administration of the said house or college, wear only the dress of secular clerics, and live most fully subject to the ordinary of the place. We moreover absolutely forbid them to put others in the place of those who fail; to acquire any new house or place, according to the decrees of the council of Lyons; or to have power to alienate the houses, effects and places which they now hold. Rather they may be gathered into one house or several, regard being had to the members who remain, so that the houses left empty may be converted to pious uses, according as shall seem, in due place and time, rightly and duly suited to the sacred canons, the will of the founders, the increase of divine worship, the salvation of souls and the public benefit. And meanwhile some man of the secular clergy, endowed with prudence and upright character, shall be designated to preside over the government of the said houses, the name of the Society being wholly deleted and suppressed.

units.orig: Declaramus individuos ctiam praedicta Societatis ex omnibus Provinciis, a quibus jam reperiuntur expulsi , comprehensos esse in hacgenerali Societatis suppressione : ac proinde volumus, quod supradicti expulsi , etiamsi ad majores Ordines sint , et existant promoti ,. nisi ad alium regularem Ordinem transierint , ad statum Clericorum et Presbyterorum Saecularium ipso facto redigantur, et Locorum Ordinariis totaliter subjiciantur.
units.en: We declare that the individual members of the said Society from all the provinces from which they are found already expelled are also comprehended in this general suppression of the Society; and therefore We will that the aforesaid expelled members, even if promoted to major orders, unless they pass to another regular order, be by the fact itself reduced to the state of secular clerics and priests, and be totally subject to the ordinaries of the places.

units.orig: Locorum Ordinarii, si eam, qua opus est, deprehenderint virtutem, doctrinam, morumque integritatem in iis, qui e Reguhiri Societatis Jesu Instituto ad Presbyterorum Siecularium statum in viin praesentium nostrarum litterarum transierint , poterunt eis pro suo arbitrio facultatem largiri, aut denegare excipiendi sacramentales confessiones Christi Fidelium , aut publicas ad populum habendi sacras conciones , sine qua licentia in scriptis nemo illorum iis fungi muneribus audebit. Hanc tamen facultatem iidem Episcopi , vel Locorum Ordinarii nunquam quoad extraneos iis concedent , qui in Collegiis, aut domibus antea ad Societatem pertinentibus vitam ducent, quibus proinde perpetuo interdicimus Sacramentum poenitentiae extraneis administrare , vel praedicare, quemadmodum ipae etiam Gregorius X. Praedecessor in citato generali Concilio simili modo prohibuit. Qua de re ipsorum Episcoporum oneramus conscientiam , quos memores cupimus severissimae illius rationis , quam de ovibus eorum curae commissis Deo sunt reddituri , et durissinii etiam illud judicii , quod iis, qui praesunt, supremus vivorum, et mortuorum Judex minatur.
units.en: The ordinaries of the places, if they find in those who by force of these our present letters shall have passed from the regular Institute of the Society of Jesus to the state of secular priests the virtue, learning and integrity of morals that is needed, may at their discretion grant them, or refuse them, the faculty of hearing the sacramental confessions of Christ's faithful and of preaching sacred sermons publicly to the people; without which licence in writing none of them shall dare to exercise those functions. Yet this faculty the same bishops or ordinaries of the places shall never grant, as regards those outside, to those who shall live in colleges or houses formerly belonging to the Society, to whom We accordingly perpetually forbid the administering of the sacrament of penance to outsiders, and preaching, even as Gregory X our predecessor forbade in like manner in the general council cited above. And concerning this We burden the conscience of the bishops themselves, whom We wish mindful of that most severe account which they are to render to God for the sheep committed to their care, and of that hardest judgement also with which the supreme Judge of the living and the dead threatens those who are set over others.
