units.orig: Volumus praelerea 5 quodsiquis eorum,qui Societatis Institutum profitebantur, munusexerceaterudiendi in litteris juventutem, aut Magistrum agat in aliquo CoUegio , aut schola , remotis penitus a regimine , administratione , et gubemio , iis tantum in docendi munere locus fiat perseverandi , et potestas , qui ad bene de suis laboribus sperandum signum aliquod praeseferant , et dummodo ab illis alienos se praebeant disputationibus , et doctrinae capitibus, quae sua vel laxitate , vel inanitate gravissimas contentiones , et incommoda parere solent , et procreare; nec ullo unquam tempore ad hujusmodi docendi munus ii admittantur, vel in eo , si nunc actu versantur, suam sinantur praestare operam , qui scholarum quietem , ac publicam tranquillitatem non sunt pro viribus conaervaturi.
units.en: We will moreover that if any of those who professed the Institute of the Society exercise the office of instructing youth in letters, or act as master in any college or school, they be altogether removed from its direction, administration and government; and that place and power of persevering in the office of teaching be given only to those who give some promise of good hope of their labours, and provided they show themselves strangers to those disputations and heads of doctrine which, by their laxity or their emptiness, are wont to breed and beget the gravest contentions and troubles; and that at no time whatever be admitted to such an office of teaching, or be allowed to continue their work in it if they are now actually engaged in it, those who are not likely to preserve, so far as in them lies, the quiet of the schools and the public tranquillity.

units.orig: Quod vero ad sacras attinet missiones, quarum etiam ratioue intelligenda volumus , quaecumque de Societatis suppressione diapo suimus , nobis rosorvamus, ea media constituere , quibus ei Infideliuni conversio , et dissidiorum sedatio facilius , et firmius obtineri possit , et comparari.
units.en: As to what concerns the sacred missions — with respect to which also We will that whatever We have disposed concerning the suppression of the Society be understood — We reserve to ourselves the establishing of those means by which the conversion of the infidels and the settling of dissensions may be obtained and secured with greater ease and firmness.

units.orig: Gassatis autem et penitus abrogatis , ut supra, privilegiis quibuscumqne et statutis saepedict» Societatis , declaramus ejus Socios , ubi a Domibus, et GoUegiis Societatis egressi, et ad statum Clericorum Saecularium redacti fuerint , habiles esse, et idoueos ad obtinenda juxta sacrorum canonum , et constitutionum Apostolicarura decreta, Beneficia quaecumque tam sine cura , quam cum cura, officia , dignitates , personatus , et id genus alia , ad quae omnia eis in Societate manentibus aditus fuerat penitus interclusus a felicis recordationis Gregorio PP. XIII. per suas in simili forma Brevis die i 0. Septembris 1 584. expeditas litteras, quarum initium est : Satis superque. Item iisdem permittimus , quod pariter vetitum eis erat , ut eleemosynam pro Missse celebratione valeant percipere ; possintque iis omnibus frui gratiis, etfavoribus, quibus tamquam Glerici Regulares Societatis Jesu perpetuo caruissent. Derogamus pariter omnibus, et singulis facultatibus , quibus a Praeposito generali , aliisque Superioribus vi privilegiorum a Summis Pontificibus obtentorum, donati fuerint, legendi videlicet haereticorum libros, et alios ab Apostolica Sede proscriptos, et damnatos; non servandi jejuniorum dies, aut esurialibus cibis in iis non utendi; anteponendi , postponendique Horarum CaQonicarum recitationem , aliisque id genus , quibus in posterum eos uti posse severissime prohibemus; cum mens nobis animusque sit, ut itidem tamquam Saeculares Presbyteri ad juris communis tramites suam accommodent vivendi rationem.
units.en: The privileges and statutes whatsoever of the oft-named Society being annulled and utterly abrogated, as above, We declare its members, when they shall have left the houses and colleges of the Society and been reduced to the state of secular clerics, to be capable and fit — according to the decrees of the sacred canons and the apostolic constitutions — to obtain any benefices whatsoever, without cure as with cure, offices, dignities, personates and other things of that kind, to all of which, while they remained in the Society, access had been utterly closed to them by Gregory XIII of happy memory, by his letters in like form of Brief expedited the 10th of September 1584, whose beginning is Satis superque. Likewise We permit them, what had equally been forbidden them, to receive an alms for the celebration of Mass, and to enjoy all those graces and favours of which, as regular clerks of the Society of Jesus, they would have been perpetually deprived. We derogate equally from each and all of the faculties with which, by force of privileges obtained from the Supreme Pontiffs, they had been endowed by the superior general and other superiors — namely of reading the books of heretics and others proscribed and condemned by the Apostolic See; of not observing the days of fasting, or of not using the foods of abstinence on them; of anticipating or postponing the recitation of the canonical hours; and other things of that kind — which We most severely forbid them to use hereafter; since it is our mind and intention that henceforth, as secular priests, they conform their manner of life to the paths of the common law.

units.orig: Vetamus,ne postquam praesentes nostrae litterae promulgatae fuerint , ac notae redditae , ullus audeat earum executionem suspendere etiam colore, titulo, praetextu cujusvis petitionis , appellationis, recursus, declarationis, aut consultationis dubiorum, quae forte oriri possent, alioque quovis praetextu praeviso, vel non praeviso. Yoiumus enim ex nunc, et inunediate suppressionem, et cassationem universae praedictae Societatis , et omnium ejus officiorum suum effectum sortiri, forma, et modo a Nobis supra expressis, sub poena majoris excommunicationis ipso facto incurrendae Nobis , nostrisque successoribus Romanis Pontificibus pro tempore reservatae adversus quemcumque , qui nostris hisce litteris adimplendis impedimentum , obicem , aut moram apponere praesumpaerit.
units.en: We forbid that, after these our present letters have been promulgated and made known, anyone dare to suspend their execution, even under the colour, title or pretext of any petition, appeal, recourse, declaration or consultation of doubts which might perhaps arise, or any other pretext foreseen or not foreseen. For We will that from this moment and immediately the suppression and annulment of the whole of the said Society and of all its offices take its effect, in the form and manner expressed by Us above, under pain of greater excommunication to be incurred by the fact itself, reserved to Us and to our successors the Roman Pontiffs for the time being, against whoever shall presume to place an impediment, obstacle or delay in the way of the fulfilment of these our letters.

units.orig: Mandamus insuper, ac in virtute sanctae obedientiae praecipimus omnibus, et singulis personis Ecclesiasticis, regularibus, saecularibus cujuscumque gradus, dignitatis, qualitatis et conditionis, et iis signanter, qui usque adhuc Societati fuerunt adscripti , et inter Socios habiti ne defendere audeant , impugnare scribere, vel etiam loqui de hujusmodi suppressione , deque ejus causis, et motivis, quemadmodum nec de Societatis Instituto, regulis Constitutionibus , regiminis forma aliave de re, quae ad hujusmodi pertinet argumentum absque expressa Romani Pontificislicentia; ac simili modo sub poena excommunicationis Nobis, ac nostris pro tempore successoribus reservatae prohibemus omnibus , et singulis y ne hujus suppressionis occasione ullum audeant , multoque minus eos , qui Socii fuerunt injuriis, jurgiis, contumeliis, aliove contemptus genere, voce, aut scripto, clam , aut palam afficere , ac lacessere.
units.en: We command moreover, and in virtue of holy obedience We enjoin, each and every ecclesiastical person, regular and secular, of whatever grade, dignity, quality and condition, and signally those who up to now were enrolled in the Society and counted among its members, not to dare to defend, to attack, to write or even to speak about this suppression, or about its causes and motives, as neither about the Institute of the Society, its rules, constitutions, form of government or any other matter pertaining to this argument, without the express licence of the Roman Pontiff; and in like manner, under pain of excommunication reserved to Us and to our successors for the time being, We forbid each and all, on occasion of this suppression, to dare to wound or provoke anyone — least of all those who were members — with injuries, taunts, insults or any other kind of contempt, by voice or in writing, secretly or openly.

units.orig: Hortamar omnes Christianos Principes, ut ea qua pollent , vi , auctoritate , et potentia , quam pro sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae. defensione, et patrocinio a Deo acceperunt, tumetiam eo, quo in hanc Apostolicam Sedem ducuntur obsequio , et cultu , suam praestent operam , ac studia , ut hae nostrae litterae suum plenissime consequantur effectum , quinimo singulis in iisdem litteris contentis inhaerentes similia constituant et promulgent decreta, per quae omnino caveant, ne , dum haec nostra voluntas executioni tradetur, ulla inter Fideles excitentur jurgia , contentiones , et dissidia.
units.en: We exhort all Christian princes that, with that force, authority and power which they have received from God for the defence and patronage of the holy Roman Church, and likewise with that obedience and reverence by which they are drawn toward this Apostolic See, they lend their labour and endeavour that these our letters obtain their fullest effect; and indeed that, adhering to each of the things contained in the same letters, they establish and promulgate similar decrees, by which they may altogether prevent any quarrels, contentions and discords from being stirred up among the faithful while this our will is carried into execution.

units.orig: Hortamur denique Christianos omnes , ac per Domini nostri Jesu Christi viscera obsecramus , ut memores sint , omnes eumdem habere Magistrum , qui in coelis est ; eumdem omnes Reparatorem , a quo empti sumus pretio magno ; eodem omnes lavacro aquae in verbo vitae regeneratos esse , et filios Dei , cohaeredes autem Christi constitutos ; eodem Catholicae doctrinae , verbique divini pabulo nutritos ; omnes demummium corpus ese in Christo, singulos autem alterum alterius membra ; atque idcirco necesse omnino esse , ut omnes communi charitatis vinculo simul colligati cum omnibus hominibus pacem habeant, ac nemini debeant quidquam , nisi ut invicem diligant ; nam qui diligit proximum , legem implevit; summo prosequentes odio offensiones, simultates, jurgia, insidias, aliaque hujusmodi ab antiquo humani generis hoste excogitata , inventa , et excitata ad Ecclesiam Dei perturbandam , impediendamque aetemam Fidelium felicitatem sub fallacissimo scholarum , opinionum , vel etiam Christianae perfectionis titulo, ac praetextu. Otnnes tandem totis viribus contendant veram , germanamque sibi sapientiam comparare , de qua scriptum est per Sanctum Jacobum cap. 3. Epist. Canon. vers. 18. « Quis sapiens, et disciplinatlis inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiae. Quod si zelum animarum habetis, et oontentiones sint in cordibus vestris , nolite gloriari j et mendaces esse adversus veritatem. Non est enim ista sapientia desursum descendens; sedterrenaanimaiis, diabolica. Ubi enim zelus, et contentio, ibi inconstantia, et omne opus pravum. QuflB autemdesursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica modesta suadibilis , bonis conaentiens , plena misericordia , et fructibus bonis, non judicans , sine smulatione. Fructus autem jiistitiffi in pace seminatur facientibns pacem. »
units.en: Lastly We exhort all Christians, and beseech them through the bowels of our Lord Jesus Christ, to remember that all have the same Master, who is in heaven; the same Redeemer, by whom we were bought at a great price; that all were regenerated in the same laver of water in the word of life, and made sons of God and co-heirs of Christ; that all were nourished with the same food of Catholic doctrine and of the divine word; that all, finally, are one body in Christ, and severally members one of another; and that therefore it is altogether necessary that all, bound together by the common bond of charity, keep peace with all men, and owe no man anything but to love one another — for he who loves his neighbour has fulfilled the law — pursuing with the utmost hatred offences, rivalries, quarrels, snares and other things of that kind, devised, invented and stirred up by the ancient enemy of the human race to disturb the Church of God and hinder the eternal happiness of the faithful, under the most deceitful title and pretext of schools, of opinions, or even of Christian perfection. Let all, in fine, strive with all their strength to acquire for themselves the true and genuine wisdom of which it is written by Saint James, in the third chapter of his canonical epistle, verse 13: 'Who is a wise man, and endued with knowledge among you? Let him show, by a good conversation, his work in the meekness of wisdom. But if you have bitter zeal, and there be contentions in your hearts, glory not, and be not liars against the truth. For this is not wisdom descending from above, but earthly, sensual, devilish. For where envying and contention is, there is inconstancy and every evil work. But the wisdom that is from above first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good, full of mercy and good fruits, without judging, without dissimulation. And the fruit of justice is sown in peace, to them that make peace.'

units.orig: Praesentes quoque litteras etiain ex eo quod Superiores , et alii religiosi saepedictae Societatis , et ceteri quicumque in praemissis interesse habentes , seu habere quomodolibet praetendentes illis non conaenaerint , nec ad ea vocati , et auditi fuerint , nullo unquam tempore de subreptionis, obreptionis , nullitatis, aut invaliditatis vitio , seu intentionis nostrae , aut alio quovis defectu etiam quantumvis magno, inexcogitato , et substantiali , sive etiam ex eo quod in praemissis seu eorum aliquo solenmitates , et quaevis alia servanda, et adimplenda servata non fuerint ; aut ex qiiocumque alio capite a jure vel consuetudine aliqua resultante etiam in corpore juris clauso j seu etiam enormis enormissims , et totalis Isesionis, et quovis alio praetextu, occasione , vel causa y etiam quantumvis justa , rationabili , et privilegiata, etiam tali , quas ad effectum validitatis praemissorum necessario exprimenda foret, notari, impugnari, invalidari retractari, in jus , Vel controversiam revocari y aut ad terminos juris reduoi , vel adversus illas restitutionis in integrum , aperitionis oris , reductionis ad viam, et terminos juris , aut aliud quodcumque juris, facti, gratis, vel justitiffi remedium impetrari , seu quomodolibet conceisso , aut impetrato quempiam uti, seu se juvari in judicio, vel extra illud posse; sed easdem praesentes semper, perpetuoque validas , firmas , et efficaces existere et fore , suosque plenarios , et integros effectus sortiri , ct obtinere, ac per omnes et singulos, ad quos spectat, et quomodolibet spectabit in futurum inviolabiliter obaervari.
units.en: We will also that these present letters can at no time ever be noted, impugned, invalidated or retracted, called into law or controversy, or reduced to the terms of law — not even on the ground that the superiors and other religious of the oft-named Society, and any others whosoever having, or in any way pretending to have, an interest in the premises, did not consent to them, nor were called and heard concerning them — nor on the ground of any vice of surreption, obreption, nullity or invalidity, or of any defect of our intention, or any other defect however great, unthought-of and substantial; nor because the solemnities and whatever else ought to have been observed and fulfilled in the premises, or any of them, were not observed; nor from any other head resulting from law or from any custom, even one contained in the body of the law; nor on the plea of enormous, most enormous and total lesion, or any other pretext, occasion or cause, however just, reasonable and privileged, even such as would necessarily have had to be expressed for the validity of the premises; nor may a restitution in integrum, an opening of the mouth, a reduction to the way and terms of law, or any other remedy of law, of fact, of grace or of justice be sought against them, or, if granted or obtained, may anyone use it or avail himself of it in court or out of it; but that these same present letters exist and shall be always and perpetually valid, firm and efficacious, obtain their plenary and entire effects, and be inviolably observed by each and all whom they concern or shall in any way concern in the future.

units.orig: Sicque, et non aliter in praemissis omnibus, et singulis per quoscumque Judices Ordinarios , et Delegatos , eliam causarum Palatii Apostolici Auditores , ac S. R. E. Cardinales , etiam de Latere Legatos, et Sedis Apostolic» Nnncios , et alios quavis auctoritate , et potestate fungentes et f uncturos in quavis causa , et instantia , sublata eis , et eorum cuilibet quavis aliter judicandi , seu interpretandi facultate , et auctoritate judicari, ac definiri debere , ac irritum, et inaae , si secus super his a quoquamquavis auctoritate , soienter, vel igaoranter contigerit attentari , decernimus.
units.en: And thus, and not otherwise, in each and all of the premises, do We decree that judgement and decision must be given by any judges whatsoever, ordinary and delegated, even the auditors of causes of the Apostolic Palace and the Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, even legates a latere and nuncios of the Apostolic See, and any others of whatever authority and power, now and hereafter exercising office, in any cause and instance — every faculty and authority of judging or interpreting otherwise being withdrawn from them and from each of them; and whatever may happen to be attempted to the contrary in these matters, by anyone, with whatever authority, knowingly or in ignorance, We decree null and void.

Quibus omnibus et singulis, etiamsi pro illorum sufficienti darogatione de illis, eorumque totis tcnoribus specialis expressa, et individua, ac de verbo ad verbum, non autem per clausulas generales idem importantes mentio , seu quaevis alia expressio habenda, aut aliqua alia exquisita forma ad hoc servanda foret, illorum omnium, et singulorum tenores, ac si dc verbo ad verbuni nihil penitus omisso, et forma in illis tradita obaervata exprimerentur, et inaererentur, praesentibus proplene, et sufficienter expressis et inaertis habentes, illis alias in $uo robore permansuris ad praemissoruni effectum specialiter, et expresse derogamus, cffiterisque contrariis quibuscumque.
units.en: Notwithstanding apostolic constitutions and ordinances, even those published in general councils, and, so far as need be, our rule of not taking away a right acquired, and likewise the statutes and customs of the oft-named Society and of its houses, colleges and churches, even strengthened by oath, apostolic confirmation or any other firmness; and the privileges also, the indults and the apostolic letters granted, confirmed and renewed to the same Society, its superiors, religious and any persons whatsoever, under whatever tenors and forms, and with whatever derogatories of derogatories and other decrees even of annulment, even motu proprio, even consistorially, or otherwise in any way. All and each of which — even if for their sufficient derogation a special, express and individual mention of them and of their whole tenors, word for word, and not by general clauses importing the same, or any other exquisite form, ought to be observed for this — holding their tenors as fully and sufficiently expressed and inserted in these presents, as if they were expressed and inserted word for word with nothing at all omitted and the form given in them observed, they otherwise to remain in their force, We specially and expressly derogate for the effect of the premises, and all other things whatsoever to the contrary.

units.orig: Volumus autem, ut praesentium iitterarum transumptis, etiam impressis, manu alicujus Notarii publici subscriptis , et sigillo alicujus personae in dignitate ecclesiastica constituts munitis, eadem prorsus fides in judicio , et extra adhibeatur, quae praesentibus ipsis adhiberetur, si forent exhibitae, vel ostensae. Datum Romae apud 5. Mariam Majorem sub annulo Piscatoris, die 2 1 julii 1773, pontificatus nostri anno quinto,
units.en: And We will that to transcripts of these present letters, even printed, subscribed by the hand of some public notary and furnished with the seal of some person constituted in ecclesiastical dignity, entirely the same faith be given, in court and out of it, as would be given to these presents themselves, if they were exhibited or shown. Given at Rome, at Saint Mary Major, under the ring of the Fisherman, the 21st day of July 1773, in the fifth year of our pontificate.
